summary: PASS=106, FAIL=0, NOT_VERIFIABLE_OFFLINE=1, N/A=3 (110 checks covering 120 individual on-chain writes). Every input field that the three configure scripts consume converts to exactly the value found in the 260902 tx-fork snapshot (120/120 by key hash + type), the 12 remaining unset=false chain entries are all attributed to MarketFactory.createMarket (via ensureMarket), Ignition Fx100Fee/Fx100Role/Fx100Oracle, or the Config.sol timestamp side effect of configureOracle, and the IfNeeded guards therefore imply a zero-applied rerun at snapshot block 46282993.
caveats: Zero-applied is proven only against the snapshot state at block 46282993 (2026-09-02T07:47:33Z). Any later write flips it: in particular env:init:mock re-points PRICE_FEED(USDC) to a shared 8-decimal USDC mock oracle (deploy-contracts.ts:579-580 comment), after which a configureOracle rerun with the current oracle.fork.tx-fork.json (oracleDecimals 18, feedAddress = Ignition MockUSDCOracle 0x2888..) would APPLY two writes and revert PRICE_FEED(USDC)/PRICE_FEED_MULTIPLIER(USDC) to 1e36 — exactly the 2026-09-01 incident the deploy script warns about.

The dump probes each key under several value types (173 keys carry >1 typed entry; e.g. POSITION_IMPACT_EXPONENT_FACTOR has a set uint probe = 1e30 and an unset bytes32 probe = 0x0). Any consumer that matches by key alone without the type will misread these as unset; the comparison here matched on key + written type.

PRICE_FEED_MULTIPLIER for the synthetic BTC index token is 1e34 because configureOracle.ts:29-31 hard-codes 18 token decimals for every non-USDC token, while the deployment manifest declares indexTokenDecimals 8 for MockBTC. The chain matches the script (so the configure reproduction PASSes), but whether 1e34 is the semantically intended normalisation for an 8-decimal synthetic index was not evaluated here.

8 expected values are 0 (SEQUENCER_GRACE_DURATION, MIN_ADDITIONAL_GAS_FOR_EXECUTION, MIN_HANDLE_EXECUTION_ERROR_GAS, MIN_HANDLE_EXECUTION_ERROR_GAS_TO_FORWARD, POSITION_IMPACT_FACTOR x4); they show as unset=true on chain, which is the correct outcome (setXIfNeeded never sends a tx when current 0 == next 0), not evidence that the field was applied.

The contracts-repo parseDecimalToScaled silently truncates fractions longer than the scale, whereas deploy-contracts.ts parseDecimalScaled (line 136-144) throws; no input in the four files exceeds its scale, so the two never diverge for this run.

GENERAL_DEFAULTS and MARKET_DEFAULTS_BY_SYMBOL (defaults.ts) are fully shadowed because every consumed field is present in the input files; the only visible override is liquidationGraceTier0Multiplier (default 8e18, input 1 -> 1e18 on chain).

ORACLE_PROVIDER_UPDATED_AT(USDC, ChainlinkPriceFeedProvider)=1788334905 is a block.timestamp and cannot be derived offline; it is 312 s before the snapshot block timestamp, consistent with the configure step running shortly before the dump. On a rerun no new timestamp is written because writers.ts:140-142 returns early when the fee-handler provider already matches.

oracle.fork.tx-fork.json is an untracked, generated file (deploy-contracts.ts:605-623 rewrites it every run from deployed addresses); its addresses were confirmed equal to the snapshot deployed-addresses.json and the manifest, and the snapshot deployed-addresses.json is byte-identical to ignition/deployments/tx-fork-v032-260902r3/deployed_addresses.json.

Not opened, per ground rules: any .env*, pk.txt, mnemonic, noise-traders.json, hardhat.fork.config.ts, Devconfig/, or the ignition fork parameters file; role grants (roles.json) were out of scope for this task.
